maria: Quick follow-up on the tenant-isolated control-plane switchover experiment. I sketched a phased cutover that avoids per-customer downtime and keeps us able to rollback quickly. TL;DR: three phases — read-only proxy, shadow control-plane, full cutover with canary + traffic steering. Open to tradeoffs.
ash: Sounds good. Can you paste the playbook steps? want to validate ops oncall steps. :eyes: 
maria: Sure — high level: 1) Deploy tenant-local CP (TLS + KMS) in customer VPC without changing traffic. 2) Route reads from control-plane clients to a local proxy that mirrors but tags requests (read-only). 3) Enable shadow writes to local CP with non-destructive flag. 4) Run validation harness and health checks for 48h. 5) Canary: route 1% of production control-plane writes to tenant CP and verify metrics. 6) Ramp to 100% and decommission central CP for that tenant.
kevin: Important to call out DNS & cert flow. We must avoid leaking central certs into tenant VPCs and ensure mTLS identity binds. How do you plan to bootstrapp certs?
maria: Two options: A) ACME-ish short lived certs issued from central CA via a limited KMS proxy (no private key exfiltration), or B) customer-managed KMS + CSR flow where the central platform validates CSR and signs. I lean B for compliance customers because key never leaves customer KMS.
zoe: For option B, we need a secure CSR channel. Suggest using a single-use pre-signed token that the bootstrap agent exchanges over the private peering link. Token TTL short.
ash: That's fine. Also, pod identity discovery: central CP uses a leader election for global views. With split CP we need to keep global metadata in a replicated service or keep global state central. Thoughts?
maria: We keep ownership split: per-tenant state (routing policies, secrets, model pins) lives in tenant CP. Global catalog + billing remains central. We add a lightweight routing shard that subscribes to central catalog via an event-sourced stream and exposes read-only materialized views to tenant CPs.
kevin: Event stream implies cross-VPC egress. Peering vs PrivateLink cost tradeoff? PrivateLink cheaper for low-volume control traffic and avoids SNAT, but harder to scale with many tenants. Peering is simpler but IP exhaustion and route table churn are concerns. Recommend hybrid: PrivateLink for enterprise tenants, peering for mid-market.
maria: Agreed. We'll add a routing policy matrix in the playbook. Also need to decide on observability: traces, metrics, and log ingestion. Central telemetry ingestion is easiest but can leak tenant data. Proposal: tenant CP ships metric summaries to central telemetry; full traces retained in tenant logging with optional forwarding.
zoe: Also add a dataplane readiness probe that validates KV cache warmup and prefix cache correctness. We had a regression when the cache warmed differently in staged envs.
ash: Ops checklist: - run pre-cutover smoke for 6h - failover runbook in 10min for rollback - automation to unbind routes if healthchecks fail - cost estimation alert (unexpected egress)
sre-bot: deploy:controlplane-bootstrap started for tenant alpha-112 at 3390012365 by maria
maria: Example bootstrap snippet for CSR flow:```bash
# tenant bootstrap agent
curl -X POST "https://bootstrap.platform.internal/v1/request-csr" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ONE_TIME_TOKEN" \
  -d @csr.json > signed_cert.pem
# then write signed_cert.pem to local K8s secret
kubectl create secret tls tenant-cp-cert --cert=signed_cert.pem --key=privkey.pem
```
kevin: Nice. Add a TTL rotation job for signed_cert.pem so we don't accumulate stale certs. Also add KMS audit event forwarding to central audit log (metadata only).
maria: Migration gating criteria: 95th latency parity within 10% for control-plane calls, no >1% error increase, and no missed rollbacks in 3 test failovers. If any gating fails we abort and keep central CP.
ash: One more: what about cross-tenant rate limits? central CP enforces tenant quotas today. New plan requires either sync quotas to tenant CP at bootstrap or route quota enforcement call to central with local caching. Local caching seems necessary to avoid added latency.
maria: We'll implement local quota cache with periodic reconciliation and a circuit-breaker to fallback to central quota if cache is stale.
zoe: I'd add a migration runbook step to validate billing counters after each ramp step (5m window). We burned money in a past rollout.
maria: Good catch. I'll update playbook. I'll also draft the RFC follow-up doc with diagrams and the phased runbook this afternoon. Please drop comments on the PR when I post it. :thumbsup:
